title: Target one Claude Code harness per project instead of writing bridges unconditionally
description: opum-agent OPAG-41 requires this repo file its half of the upstream fix before AGENTS.md can be deleted fleet-wide: lore init and lore agents write Claude, Codex and AGENTS.md bridges unconditionally rather than targeting one harness per project, and skills should distribute via the marketplace (the opum-lore plugin, LCLI-441) while init primes only the CLAUDE.md block. This also relates to LCLI-437 (agents --check drift on a Codex-only init) and is the concrete blocker recorded on LCLI-439/LCLI-438: this repo cannot delete its own AGENTS.md or .codex/ until this lands, because AGENTS.md is currently the only home for the Quest-managed instructions block (quest agents --check --require-installed reads it there) and the only Codex-bridge selection signal lore agents --check inspects.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore init defaults to one selected harness (Claude or Codex) rather than writing both bridges unconditionally
lore agents --check reports a consistent result for a Claude-only, a Codex-only, and a both-bridges repository without requiring the unselected bridge
Once this lands, lore-cli AGENTS.md and .codex/ can be deleted without breaking quest agents --check --require-installed or lore agent-bridge product behavior

implementationNotes: Correction: AC#1 (lore init defaults to one selected harness) is NOT satisfied by this pass and I incorrectly checked it initially -- uncorrected here. The fix landed only changes lore agents' CHECK/regeneration consistency (AC#2, now genuinely verified), not lore init's own wizard, which still prompts Set up the Claude bridge? and Set up the Codex bridge? independently and defaults both to yes on Enter -- a user can still end up with both bridges by accident through the interactive flow. AC#1 and AC#3 (AGENTS.md/.codex deletion safety, which also needs quest-cli's side of the fix for the managed-instructions-block-lives-only-in-AGENTS.md problem) remain open. This task is not fully done; reporting the honest split rather than closing early.

AC#1 landed, additively: the interactive wizard's Codex prompt (src/commands/init.ts runInteractiveWizard) now defaults to declining once the Claude prompt was already accepted (!wantAgents), instead of always defaulting to accepting. A bare Enter through both prompts with both agent CLIs detected now selects Claude only, matching one-harness-per-project. Preserved: Claude declined or not offered -> Codex still defaults to accepting (today's behavior, unchanged); an explicit yes to Codex still selects both regardless of Claude's answer -- this only changes what a bare Enter means, never removes the choice. Flag-driven init (--agents/--codex, already independently opt-in) is untouched. 4 new tests in test/init.test.ts proving: Claude-accepted flips Codex's default to false, Claude-declined leaves Codex's default at true, an explicit yes to Codex still works after Claude, and Codex-only availability is unaffected. Verified no pre-existing test relied on the old default (every test exercising both-available already answered the Codex question explicitly). Full suite 2818 pass/1 skip/0 fail, typecheck clean, lint clean (biome auto-fixed one line-width wrap in the new code), lore check 76 files/0 errors. AC#1 now checked. AC#3 (AGENTS.md/.codex deletion) remains open, still gated on quest-cli's own fix.

quest 0.3.3 published, adding --target claude/codex to quest agents (per opum-agent). Ran: npm i -g @opum-ai/quest@0.3.3 (already at 0.3.3 on this machine), quest agents --update-instructions --target claude, quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude (exit 0). Verified: only CLAUDE.md changed (6 insertions, its own quest:agent-instructions block refreshed to reference Quest CLI 0.3.3 and the --target claude check invocation); no AGENTS.md write happened; the fleet operating block digest is unchanged (9eddf7883da91a63, matches CI's EXPECTED_DIGEST exactly); lore check 76 files/0 errors. The DEFAULT (--target omitted, meaning codex/AGENTS.md) quest agents --check --require-installed now correctly reports drift, since AGENTS.md's own block is untouched and stale relative to 0.3.3 -- expected and acceptable, since AGENTS.md is now the target-claude-migrated repo's LEGACY location pending deletion, not the active one. This resolves the quest-side half of AC#3's blocker. The lore-side half (agents.ts's hasClaudeBridge/hasCodexBridge) already landed. Remaining before AC#3 can be checked: actually delete AGENTS.md and .codex/, which needs my user's explicit approval (same as quest-cli did for their own AGENTS.md deletion), then confirm lore agents --check proposes nothing Codex-shaped afterward.
